#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Test edge cases for the NamedTuple implementation.
"""

from collections import namedtuple
from scim2_filter_parser import attr_paths as attr_paths_mod

def test_namedtuple_properties():
    """Test that our NamedTuple behaves correctly"""
    print("=== TESTING NAMEDTUPLE PROPERTIES ===")
    
    # Test that it's actually a namedtuple
    AttrPathTuple = namedtuple('AttrPathTuple', ['attr_name', 'sub_attr', 'uri'])
    test_tuple = AttrPathTuple('test', 'sub', 'http://example.com')
    
    print(f"NamedTuple: {test_tuple}")
    print(f"Type: {type(test_tuple)}")
    print(f"Is tuple subclass: {isinstance(test_tuple, tuple)}")
    
    # Test all access methods
    assert test_tuple[0] == 'test'
    assert test_tuple[1] == 'sub' 
    assert test_tuple[2] == 'http://example.com'
    
    assert test_tuple.attr_name == 'test'
    assert test_tuple.sub_attr == 'sub'
    assert test_tuple.uri == 'http://example.com'
    
    # Test that it's iterable
    values = list(test_tuple)
    assert values == ['test', 'sub', 'http://example.com']
    
    # Test equality with regular tuple
    regular_tuple = ('test', 'sub', 'http://example.com')
    assert test_tuple == regular_tuple
    print("✓ NamedTuple equals regular tuple with same values")
    
    print("✓ All NamedTuple properties work correctly")

def test_real_world_usage():
    """Test real-world usage scenarios"""
    print("\n=== TESTING REAL-WORLD USAGE ===")
    
    attr_map = {
        ('userName', None, None): 'username',
        ('name', 'familyName', None): 'family_name',
        ('emails', 'type', None): 'emails.type',
        ('emails', 'value', None): 'emails.value',
        ('meta', 'lastModified', 'urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:core:2.0:User'): 'last_modified',
    }
    
    # Complex query with multiple attribute types
    query = '''userName eq "john.doe" and name.familyName co "Doe" and 
               emails[type eq "work" and value co "@company.com"]'''
               
    attr_paths = attr_paths_mod.AttrPath(query, attr_map)
    
    path_list = list(attr_paths)
    print(f"Found {len(path_list)} attribute paths:")
    
    for i, path in enumerate(path_list):
        print(f"  {i}: {path}")
        print(f"     attr_name: {path.attr_name}")
        print(f"     sub_attr: {path.sub_attr}")
        print(f"     uri: {path.uri}")
        
        # Verify all access methods work
        assert path[0] == path.attr_name
        assert path[1] == path.sub_attr
        assert path[2] == path.uri
        
    # Test first_path property
    first_path = attr_paths.first_path
    print(f"\nFirst path: {first_path}")
    print(f"  Access by name: attr_name={first_path.attr_name}, sub_attr={first_path.sub_attr}, uri={first_path.uri}")
    print(f"  Access by index: [0]={first_path[0]}, [1]={first_path[1]}, [2]={first_path[2]}")
    
    assert first_path.attr_name == first_path[0]
    assert first_path.sub_attr == first_path[1]
    assert first_path.uri == first_path[2]
    
    print("✓ Real-world usage works correctly")

def test_none_values():
    """Test handling of None values"""
    print("\n=== TESTING NONE VALUES ===")
    
    attr_map = {
        ('simpleAttr', None, None): 'simple_attr',
        ('complexAttr', 'subAttr', None): 'complex.sub_attr',
        ('schemaAttr', None, 'urn:example'): 'schema_attr',
    }
    
    query = 'simpleAttr eq "value"'
    attr_paths = attr_paths_mod.AttrPath(query, attr_map)
    
    for path in attr_paths:
        print(f"Path: {path}")
        print(f"  attr_name: {repr(path.attr_name)} (type: {type(path.attr_name)})")
        print(f"  sub_attr: {repr(path.sub_attr)} (type: {type(path.sub_attr)})")
        print(f"  uri: {repr(path.uri)} (type: {type(path.uri)})")
        
        # Test None comparisons
        assert path.sub_attr is None or isinstance(path.sub_attr, str)
        assert path.uri is None or isinstance(path.uri, str)
        
    print("✓ None values handled correctly")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    test_namedtuple_properties()
    test_real_world_usage()
    test_none_values()
    print("\n🎉 ALL EDGE CASE TESTS PASSED! 🎉")
